reasoning: Recent general-election polling in Michigan’s 2026 Senate race between Republican Mike Rogers and Democrat Abdul El-Sayed shows Republicans with a small but consistent edge, while major forecasters currently rate the race as a toss-up. Within the last 45 days, three separate statewide polls all have Rogers ahead of El‑Sayed by margins of roughly 3 to 10 points, suggesting a current R+3 to R+5 environment in the Senate race, albeit within a highly competitive context; there are no comparable recent general-election polls for the presidential race in this window.

sources.name: Breitbart report on Glengariff Group statewide Michigan poll
sources.details: Statewide Glengariff Group poll for Michigan Education Association/Business Leaders for Michigan found Mike Rogers leading Abdul El-Sayed 49% to 39% in a hypothetical Senate matchup, a 10-point Republican advantage.

sources.name: Jewish Insider report on Glengariff Group Michigan Senate poll
sources.details: Jewish Insider summary of the same Glengariff Group poll notes Rogers leading El-Sayed 48% to 41% and Stevens leading Rogers 47% to 45% among definite general-election voters, underscoring a modest but real edge for Rogers over El-Sayed.

sources.name: Newsweek summary of EPIC-MRA Michigan Senate poll
sources.details: EPIC-MRA statewide poll of 600 Michigan voters found Mike Rogers leading Abdul El-Sayed 46% to 43% in the U.S. Senate race, a 3-point Republican advantage.

sources.name: Newsweek summary of Mitchell Research Michigan Senate poll
sources.details: Mitchell Research & Communications poll of 672 likely Michigan voters showed the Rogers–El-Sayed Senate race tied at 45%–45%, indicating an evenly matched contest at that time.

sources.name: WJR coverage of Glengariff Group Michigan Senate poll
sources.details: Talk radio outlet WJR’s report on the Glengariff survey reiterates that Rogers held about a 10-point lead over El-Sayed in the hypothetical Senate matchup, highlighting GOP strength against the Democratic nominee.

sources.name: Newsweek synthesis of Michigan Senate polling landscape
sources.details: Newsweek article notes that multiple polls (EPIC-MRA, Mitchell Research, Glengariff Group) show a tight but often Rogers-leaning general-election race versus El-Sayed, while describing overall dynamics as competitive.

sources.name: Washington Post summary of Fox News Michigan Senate poll
sources.details: Washington Post article reports on a Fox News statewide poll finding Michigan’s marquee Senate race between Mike Rogers and Abdul El-Sayed is close, with voters sharply divided and the contest considered critical for Senate control; the description implies a near-even race without giving a precise margin in the text quoted.

sources.name: New York Times analysis of Michigan Democratic Senate primary polling
sources.details: New York Times overview of Democratic primary polling shows Abdul El-Sayed holding double-digit leads over Haley Stevens in several independent and partisan polls of the Michigan Democratic Senate primary electorate.

sources.name: Emerson College Polling Michigan Democratic Senate primary poll
sources.details: Emerson College Polling/WLNS/WOOD TV survey of Democratic primary voters shows El-Sayed leading Stevens 54% to 39%, a 15-point advantage in the primary.

sources.name: Detroit Free Press on RealClearPolitics average and Michigan Senate primary polling
sources.details: Free Press coverage of RealClearPolitics average and individual primary polls notes El-Sayed leading Stevens by about 9–15 points across several recent Democratic primary surveys.

sources.name: MLive report on Tavern Research Michigan Democratic Senate primary poll
sources.details: MLive article on Tavern Research poll reports El-Sayed leading Stevens 46% to 36% among Democratic primary voters, a 10-point margin.

sources.name: Newsweek synthesis of Michigan Democratic Senate primary polling
sources.details: Newsweek summary of Mitchell Research Democratic primary poll shows El-Sayed up 14 points, 52% to 38%, and discusses several other primary polls all showing him ahead of Stevens, though one earlier Glengariff survey had Stevens up 7.

sources.name: Wall Street Journal report on Michigan Democratic Senate primary results
sources.details: Wall Street Journal notes that with 99% of the expected vote tallied, El-Sayed led Stevens 48.5% to 47.5% in the Democratic Senate primary, confirming his narrow victory and status as the nominee.

sources.name: NBC News Michigan Senate primary live results
sources.details: NBC News live results page shows final Michigan Democratic Senate primary tallies with El-Sayed narrowly ahead of Stevens, cementing the general-election matchup with Mike Rogers.

sources.name: Cook Political Report and Sabato’s Crystal Ball ratings via Newsweek
sources.details: Newsweek reports that both the Cook Political Report and Sabato's Crystal Ball classify the Michigan Senate race as a toss-up at this stage, reflecting no clear structural advantage for either party beyond normal partisan lean.
